dependencies.basis: Business Register methodology: 'Establishments are coded based on the concept of major business activity in a manner consistent with the approach outlined by the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS).'

Annual Survey of Service Industries target-population statements: establishments are classified according to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) and drawn from the Business Register by NAICS code.

Quarterly Survey of Financial Statements: enterprises are classified under the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) to the code that relates to the activity providing the most value-added. Series from Q1 2023 forward based on NAICS 2022.

Canadian International Merchandise Trade (Customs Basis) and CIMT commodity classification documentation: merchandise is classified under the Harmonized System (HS), extended to 8 digits for exports and 10 digits for imports; unit-value edits applied by HS code.
Discharge Abstract Database metadata: 'Since 2004–2005, all DAD records have been reported in ICD-10-CA and CCI.' Canadian Coding Standards for ICD-10-CA and CCI apply to DAD and NACRS submissions.

Labour Force Survey classification statement: 'The LFS uses the 2021 National Occupational Classification (NOC) v1.0 and estimates of employment are coded up to the five-digit level.' Also coded to NAICS 2022.
Labour Force Survey: industry estimates coded using the 2022 North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) v1.0 up to the four-digit level.

_notes: All edges follow the Research.1 rule: the programme names the classification; the classification document itself is not treated as the source of the edge.
Business Register is the common upstream frame for many of the economic surveys that then inherit NAICS codes.
Health (ICD-10-CA/CCI) and occupational (NOC) hubs are now documented alongside the industry and commodity hubs.
No soft or financing edges introduced.
